title: Composition and IME reconciliation
goal: Composed input (dead keys, Japanese/Chinese/Korean IMEs, Android Gboard, iOS predictive/autocorrect) produces correct ledger events without any native mutation surviving outside an active composition.
scope: compositionstart: freeze rendering of the composing block; only the composing text node may change
compositionend (+ browser-specific input ordering): read the committed text, restore the DOM from state, apply ins/del via the ledger, re-render, restore the caret within the same task
Android: insertCompositionText for all typing, Gboard deletions via compositions
Korean per-syllable composition; Safari ordering quirks; cancel on blur or selection jump
Guard allowlist active only during a composition
out_of_scope: Rich IME UI (candidate windows are native)

rules.rule: I5 allowlist only for the composing node during composition; I1 holds again in the same task after compositionend.
One ledger event per committed composition (or coalesced word), never per update.

secondary: B2 ProseMirror where the driver supports composition

criteria: CDP composition scenarios (dead keys ü/é/ñ/â, Japanese kana→kanji with candidate switch, Korean, Pinyin, Escape cancel, composition replacing a cross-block selection) equal the native oracle on chromium and android-chrome.
Fuzz with composition steps: 10 000 (chromium) and 1 000 (android-chrome) sequences, 0 violations.
Android emulator: sequences typed through the real Gboard soft keyboard equal the native oracle.
iOS simulator: typing via the simulator keyboard including an autocorrect replacement and a predictive-bar tap equals the native oracle.
Firefox/WebKit desktop composition is listed as unsupported-by-driver and mapped to X-04 rows.
No ledger event per intermediate composition update.
acceptance.critic: Differential plus criteria; mobile evidence (screen recordings or step logs) is mandatory.
